title: Central Finland: 2.0 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €78,480 a year
markdown:
# Central Finland: 2.0 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €78,480 a year

> 2.0 more patients a year treated to cure · €78,480 of €1M · €921,520 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in Central Finland, 27 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. The difference is within what chance alone gives a county of this size. [^care_curative] Compared with the best quarter of counties, about 4.0 patients a year are missing from treatment that aims to cure (range 0.0–8.5). [^model] Against Finland as a whole there is no shortfall to split. [^model][^care_curative] Central Finland operates 22.4% of patients, against 15.0% nationally. [^care_surgery]

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 27.2% to 28.7% by 2028: 2.0 more patients a year (range 0.0–2.0), for €78,480 a year, about €40,041 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €27,480 | 1.0 (0.0–2.0) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.2% → 28.0% by 2028 |
| | **Needs the collaborative area (university hospital)** | | | | |
| 2 | **Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital**[^ev_video_mdt_stage1_3_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; lead of the university hospital lung MDT | €51,000 | 1.0 (0.0–0.9) | Ask the university hospital for a fixed weekly video slot and list every stage I-III patient diagnosed last month who was not discussed there. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.2% → 27.9% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€78,480** | **2.0 (0.0–2.0)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €841,193 a year; modelled to avoid 1.5 deaths a year (0.3–3.8). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 27.2% (2019–2023, measured) → 28.7% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

The remaining €921,520 buys nothing more toward treatment to cure. [^model] More money does not help, because the measures that add to it are limited by the reachable part of the shortfall. [^model] To see what else the money could do, look at low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or rank measures by deaths avoided. [^model] Lung cancer causes about 97 deaths a year in Central Finland. [^deaths] This plan is modelled to avoid 0.3 of them (range 0.0–0.6). [^deaths][^model]

## Limits

- Effects are assumptions, not trial results. Each range runs from all assumptions at their lowest to all at their highest, and is not a probability. [^model]
- The expected share is adjusted only for residents' age, not for stage, fitness, other illness, histology, how cancer was found or smoking. County figures cannot show cause. [^model]
- The estimated symptom-to-treatment clock is not used here. 0 of 3 measured outcomes moved with it as expected beyond chance. [^model]

flagged.sentence: Against Finland as a whole there is no shortfall to split: Central Finland operates 22.4% of patients, against 15.0% nationally. [^model][^care_surgery]
flagged.reason: The colon presented the higher surgery share as the reason there is no shortfall. The shortfall concerns treatment that aims to cure (27.2% vs 27.0%), and the surgery figure comes from a different period and source. I split it into two sentences, each with its own source.

flagged.sentence: The remaining €921,520 buys nothing more toward treatment to cure.
flagged.reason: The sentence had no source marker. I added [^model], which is the source of the plan saturation figures.

flagged.sentence: More would come from low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or from ranking measures by deaths avoided. [^model]
flagged.reason: It implied these options would add more patients treated to cure. The material only lists them as other uses of the money. Measures ranked by deaths avoided do not change who gets treated to cure, and screening is not quantified for this objective. I rewrote it to match the source.

flagged.sentence: Lung cancer causes about 97 deaths a year in Central Finland.
flagged.reason: The sentence had no source marker. I added [^deaths] (Finnish Cancer Registry deaths, 2020-2024).

flagged.sentence: Shares are adjusted only for residents' age, not for stage, fitness, other illness, histology, how cancer was found or smoking. County figures cannot show cause. [^model]
flagged.reason: The measured shares are not adjusted. Only the modelled expected share (26.2%) is adjusted, for the share of residents aged 65 or over. I rewrote the sentence so measured figures are not presented as adjusted.
